Busko Zdroj Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Busko-Zdrój, Poland

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Busko's Jewish community developed after 1862 restrictions on Jewish settlement were lifted, reaching 1,464 people by 1921. During the ghetto's extermination, the Germans carried out executions at this cemetery, burying victims in mass graves; in 1943, two Polish women, Zofia Dytkowska and Helena Żurkiewicz, were also shot here for aiding partisans. In 2016, the Nissenbaum Family Foundation, with city authorities and private sponsors, cleaned and fenced the cemetery.
